# Governed Agent Architecture

A Python reference implementation for actor-scoped agent memory, retrieval, and
runtime tracing.

The project demonstrates a complete request path in which an adapter resolves an
actor, a LangGraph workflow retrieves relevant context, a model produces a
response, a salience gate decides whether the user message should become memory,
and runtime events are recorded for later inspection or offline evaluation.

The repository is a reference runtime rather than a packaged agent framework or
hosted service. Its current integrations are Python modules and local scripts;
it does not expose a public HTTP API, MCP server, or installable CLI.

## What the Project Implements

- A five-stage LangGraph workflow: identity, retrieval, model call, salience
  evaluation, and memory write.
- Explicit actor, organization, role, and session context on runtime requests.
- An in-process memory stand-in for database-free development and tests.
- Optional Postgres storage for semantic, episodic, and procedural memory.
- Full-text and vector retrieval combined with reciprocal rank fusion.
- Lightweight relationship extraction and graph-assisted memory expansion.
- Retrieval logs, runtime trace events, audit records, and diagnostic reports.
- Telegram and WhatsApp message normalization and actor resolution.
- SkillLoop-compatible JSONL trace export for offline evaluation and review.
- Optional scripts for reviewed proposal import, vault/session ingestion,
  event processing, and review notifications.

## System Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Entry["Runtime entry"]
        Python["Direct Python invocation"]
        Telegram["Telegram adapter"]
        WhatsApp["WhatsApp adapter"]
    end

    subgraph Workflow["LangGraph workflow"]
        Identity["Resolve actor identity"]
        Retrieve["Retrieve scoped context"]
        Model["Call model or local fallback"]
        Salience["Evaluate memory salience"]
        Write["Write salient memory"]
    end

    subgraph Storage["Storage and observability"]
        Local["In-process memory stand-in"]
        Typed["Postgres typed memory"]
        Graph["Memory relationships"]
        Events["Event store"]
        Telemetry["Retrieval logs and trace events"]
    end

    subgraph Offline["Optional offline integrations"]
        Export["Redacted trace export"]
        SkillLoop["SkillLoop evaluation and review"]
        Import["Reviewed proposal import"]
        Bridge["Vault and session bridge"]
    end

    Python --> Identity
    Telegram --> Identity
    WhatsApp --> Identity
    Identity --> Retrieve
    Retrieve --> Local
    Retrieve --> Typed
    Retrieve --> Graph
    Local --> Retrieve
    Typed --> Retrieve
    Graph --> Retrieve
    Retrieve --> Model --> Salience --> Write
    Write --> Local
    Write -->|"when MEMORY_BACKEND=postgres"| Typed
    Telegram -.-> Events
    WhatsApp -.-> Events
    Retrieve --> Telemetry
    Model --> Telemetry
    Telemetry --> Export --> SkillLoop
    SkillLoop -->|"human-reviewed artifacts"| Import --> Typed
    Bridge --> Typed
```

The online workflow does not depend on SkillLoop. Trace export and reviewed
proposal import are explicit offline operations; Postgres remains the canonical
durable memory store when the durable backend is enabled.

## Request Lifecycle

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User
    participant Adapter as Channel adapter
    participant Runtime as LangGraph runtime
    participant Memory as Memory stores
    participant Model as Model client
    participant Trace as Trace store

    User->>Adapter: Send message
    Adapter->>Adapter: Normalize sender and resolve actor
    Adapter->>Runtime: Invoke with actor, org, role, and session
    Runtime->>Memory: Retrieve actor-scoped context
    Memory-->>Runtime: Return ranked memories
    Runtime->>Model: Send user message and retrieved context
    Model-->>Runtime: Return response
    Runtime->>Trace: Record retrieval and model diagnostics
    Runtime->>Runtime: Evaluate memory salience
    opt Salience gate passes
        Runtime->>Memory: Store semantic memory
    end
    Runtime-->>Adapter: Return response and runtime metadata
    Adapter-->>User: Deliver response
```

## Core Components

| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `src/graph.py` | Builds and executes the five-stage LangGraph workflow. |
| `src/adapters/` | Normalizes Telegram and WhatsApp messages and resolves actors. |
| `src/hermes_native_memory.py` | Provides the current process-local memory stand-in. |
| `src/durable_memory.py` | Reads and writes typed memory in Postgres. |
| `src/hybrid_retrieval.py` | Runs FTS, optional vector search, and RRF ranking. |
| `src/graph_memory.py` | Extracts simple relationships and expands retrieval through them. |
| `src/tracing.py` | Stores runtime trace events and diagnostic reports. |
| `src/trace_export.py` | Produces SkillLoop-compatible JSONL traces. |
| `event_worker.py` | Converts queued events into typed-memory records. |
| `init_schema.sql` | Creates the Postgres schemas, tables, indexes, and RLS policies. |

## Memory Model

The Postgres schema separates three memory types:

| Type | Purpose | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Semantic | Durable facts and preferences | “The user prefers concise reports.” |
| Episodic | Time-bound interactions and events | “The user reviewed the deployment on Friday.” |
| Procedural | Reusable processes and workflows | “Run tests before creating a release.” |

Each typed-memory record also carries actor and session scope, organization,
visibility, confidence, source, metadata, expiry, and supersession fields.

The current online salience gate writes semantic facts only. Event processing,
bridge scripts, and reviewed imports can create other memory categories.

## Quick Start

Python 3.11 or later is required.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/lamenting-hawthorn/governed-agent-architecture.git
cd governed-agent-architecture

python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
```

Run the database-free checks:

```bash
python -B smoke_test.py

MEMORY_BACKEND=fake \
CHECKPOINTER=memory \
AGENT_ORG_ID=local \
python -B -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider \
  src/test_trace_export.py \
  src/test_adapters.py \
  src/test_guardrails.py \
  -q
```

Run a deterministic sample turn and create a SkillLoop-compatible trace:

```bash
python -B examples/export_skillloop_trace.py
```

The example uses the in-memory backend and local model fallback. It writes:

```text
examples/out/sample_runtime_turn_trace.jsonl
```

## Postgres-Backed Runtime

Postgres and the `pgvector` extension are required for durable memory, hybrid
vector retrieval, database tracing, and Postgres checkpointing.

```bash
createdb agent_memory
psql postgresql:///agent_memory -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f init_schema.sql

export DATABASE_URL=postgresql:///agent_memory
export MEMORY_BACKEND=postgres
export CHECKPOINTER=postgres
export AGENT_ORG_ID=local_org
```

The runtime reads configuration from the process environment. Copying
`.env.example` to `.env` is useful as a configuration reference, but the Python
runtime does not automatically load that file.

### Runtime configuration

| Variable | Purpose | Typical value |
|---|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL` | Postgres connection string | `postgresql:///agent_memory` |
| `MEMORY_BACKEND` | Selects fake or durable memory | `fake` or `postgres` |
| `CHECKPOINTER` | Selects in-memory or Postgres checkpoints | `memory` or `postgres` |
| `AGENT_ORG_ID` | Organization used during actor resolution | `local_org` |
| `LLM_API_KEY` | Enables the configured remote model | provider API key |
| `LLM_BASE_URL` | OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint | provider URL |
| `LLM_MODEL` | Model identifier sent to the endpoint | provider model name |

### Embeddings

Local sentence-transformer embeddings are the default:

```text
EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=local
LOCAL_EMBEDDING_MODEL=all-MiniLM-L6-v2
```

An OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint can be used instead:

```text
EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=openai
EMBEDDING_API_KEY=...
EMBEDDING_MODEL=text-embedding-3-small
```

The schema stores 1,536-dimensional vectors. The default local 384-dimensional
vectors are zero-padded to match that schema. Do not mix embeddings from
different providers or models in the same vector space; rebuild stored vectors
when the embedding model changes.

## SkillLoop Trace Export

Completed runtime data can be exported as redacted, normalized JSONL for
SkillLoop ingestion:

```bash
python -B examples/export_skillloop_trace.py

skillloop --path /path/to/project ingest agent-architecture \
  /path/to/governed-agent-architecture/examples/out/sample_runtime_turn_trace.jsonl
```

This boundary is intentionally offline. Exporting a trace does not allow
SkillLoop to mutate live memory. Reviewed proposals are imported separately by
`scripts/connect_skillloop.py`.

See `docs/SKILLLOOP_INGEST_EXAMPLE.md` for the complete example.

## Optional Local Operations

The repository also includes local operational scripts:

- `scripts/connect_skillloop.py` imports human-reviewed SkillLoop memory
  proposals into Postgres.
- `scripts/bridge_vault_and_sessions.py` imports selected vault content and
  Hermes session evidence.
- `scripts/drain_events.py` performs a one-shot event-store drain.
- `scripts/notify_review.py` sends a Telegram digest of review activity.
- `event_worker.py` continuously processes raw events into typed memory.
- `sync_wiki.py` imports Markdown knowledge into Postgres.

These scripts are optional and are not required for the database-free sample.

## Validation

Run the same fake-backend checks used by GitHub Actions:

```bash
MEMORY_BACKEND=fake \
CHECKPOINTER=memory \
AGENT_ORG_ID=ci_org \
EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=openai \
python -B -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider src -q

python -B smoke_test.py
ruff check .
```

The hosted CI configuration uses fake memory and in-memory checkpoints. A green
CI run therefore validates the Python workflow, adapters, trace export,
guardrails, and public-repository checks; it does not validate Postgres, schema
migration, RLS behavior, live model calls, or the optional SkillLoop connector.

## Current Scope and Limitations

This repository is a reference implementation for local development and
architecture evaluation. It is not a turnkey multi-tenant service.

- The project is not currently distributed as an installable Python package.
- The supported entry points are Python modules and scripts; no HTTP API, MCP
  server, or general-purpose CLI is included.
- Telegram and WhatsApp adapters resolve application identity but do not
  implement production channel authentication or membership verification.
- The process-local memory stand-in is reset when the Python process exits.
- The online salience gate uses phrase and identity-pattern heuristics and
  stores the original user text as semantic memory.
- Postgres access uses a service-role database context; deployment code remains
  responsible for authenticated identity and tenant-safe authorization.
- Redaction is applied in trace export and selected import/bridge paths; it is
  not a universal pre-storage filter for every runtime write.
- Postgres integration and RLS regression tests require a separately provisioned
  database and are not exercised by the default hosted CI job.

Production deployments must supply their own authenticated identity boundary,
secrets management, tenant-isolation validation, backup and recovery,
observability, migration management, retention policy, and operational runbooks.
